label: Copy-phase re-input of t/z/g/q/0/e early in the copy of long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original phase or on <DEL>) and never on the first occurrence of a token, so it fires when an original token is fed back in. Almost all of its mass (about 99%) is on fed-back inputs t, z, g, q, 0, e, with t and z strongest. It is biased toward long sequences (L=9 holds 69% of the mass) and toward the first few copy steps (recall_idx 1-3, absolute t of 10-12, peaking at recall_idx 2, where the input is orig(1)). There is a smaller bump at the last copy steps of L=9. The largest activations are t or g as the second original token being re-input. The token set alone has recall 0.98 but precision 0.12. Adding L>=8 and recall_idx<=3 raises precision to about 0.4 but drops recall to about 0.6. Conditioning on the output token did not help, so whatever decides which of these steps fire is not captured.
